anchor: Everything in this set is built from six objects and one operator.
statement: Theory 01 fixes the six-object signature of the KnowledgeOS transformation carrier: D (data, a finite multiset of records), T (transformation D->R), R=T(D) (representation), Q (inquiry D->Y), Pi (observable R->O), O (decoder R->Y), and C (constraint predicate on R), plus the inquiry frame Pi_frame=(Q,C,O) with O fixed in advance.

anchor: a record r = (value, source, tag, timestamp)
statement: A record in the tested carriers is r=(value,source,tag,timestamp), optionally a derived rank; explicitly flagged as an experimental carrier, not declared to be the mathematical carrier of KnowledgeOS.

anchor: Set subtraction D \ S is INVALID wherever a field is relative.
statement: The elimination operator E_S must be typed to the level it acts at and must recompute relative fields (e.g. within-group rank) after removing S; naive set subtraction D\S leaves stale relative values and produces a representation the level's own rules forbid.

assumptions.statement: E_S recomputes rank at the relational level in tested implementations
assumptions.anchor: the naive D∖S leaves stale ranks

anchor: Zero is indexed by (T,Π) and by the subset S; adequacy by (T,Q) and the population; realization by (T,Q,O) and the case.
statement: Zero, Adequacy and Realization are defined with different index sets and are not three readings of one quantity: Zero_{T,Pi}(S;D) <=> Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))); Adequate(T,Q) <=> Hhat(Q|T(D))=0; Realized(T,Q,O) <=> O(T(D))=Q(D).

anchor: Π and Q must read disjoint fields, and disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T), not the pair (Π, Q).
statement: An anti-circularity requirement (candidate FR-003) is proposed: read-disjointness of Pi and Q must be verified on the triple (Pi,Q,T) because T can derive an output field Pi reads from sources Pi never declared; two concrete KR-BRIDGE-02 failures (a rank field secretly shared with Q's tag field, and an arity observable secretly reading value via deduplication survivorship) show declaration is not verification.

anchor: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier.
statement: Every experiment used a deliberately small numerical carrier (|D|<=6) so fibers would collide and adequacy would be measurable; this is a calibration choice, not an ontological one, and the move to documents/claims/entities/relations/provenance/contradictions/temporal states/evidence is the open research problem.

anchor: A transformation family is either sequential (Rk+1 = Tk(Rk)) or parallel (Rk = Tk(D)) — never silently mixed
statement: Sequential vs parallel transformation families is a permanent type-discipline rule, load-bearing because the data-processing inequality (document 04) applies to sequential families and not to parallel ones.

anchor: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are three distinct questions. None implies another.
statement: The load-bearing result of the Theory 00-14 programme: Pi(T(D))=Pi(T(E_S(D))) [Zero/eliminability], Hhat(Q|T(D))=0 [Adequacy/preservation] and O(T(D))=Q(D) [Realization] are shown to differ in every system tested, by independent mechanisms; tagged [EXP] deliberately rather than [THM] because necessity of the separation in general is unproven.

experiment.hypothesis: Eliminability, Preservation and Realization are separate properties
experiment.inputs: Zero rate, RD estimates, adequacy/realization measurements
experiment.conclusion: three-question separation holds in tested systems

anchor: Eliminability does not predict Preservation
statement: Four experiments of increasing power (H-RR2 boundary-crossing Zero rate 0.0377 vs 0.0426; KR-BRIDGE-01 marginal RD=-0.363 fully explained by redundancy confounding; KR-BRIDGE-02 H1 not refuted; KR-BRIDGE-03 at 13x informative strata, H1 still not refuted, surviving cells 14->1) converge on the same negative finding, stable under a 13-fold power increase.

anchor: Preservation does not give Realization
statement: Hhat(Q|R5)=0 (adequate) is a separate fact from O(R5)=Q(D) (realized): a fixed decoder can fail on information-theoretically adequate data because it was fixed in advance and not refit; flagged as a design defect that the KR-REP-REDUCTION chain never operationalized this separation (no dropped record/source ever made constraint C fail), so 'the separation is real; that experiment could not exhibit it.'

anchor: Eliminability does not give Realization
statement: Not derivable merely from the other two separations (explicitly not a corollary): Zero is defined via Pi, which is read-disjoint from Q by construction, so it carries no information about Q's recoverability 'by design' — verified rather than assumed.

anchor: Realization ⟹ Adequacy
statement: Standing conjecture that if a fixed decoder recovers Q from R on every observed case, R determines Q on the realized cases; refutable by a decoder that is right by luck (correct on every observed case while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous); explicitly 'not tested.'

anchor: Do the separations survive a non-synthetic carrier?
statement: Flagged as the central transfer problem: whether eliminability/preservation/realization separations generalize beyond the tested synthetic carrier is explicitly open.

anchor: A representation R = T(D) is adequate for Q iff Q is determined by R: Hhat(Q|R)=0
statement: Adequacy is defined information-theoretically as zero conditional entropy of Q given R, operationalized as fiber Q-homogeneity over a population; flagged [DEFECT] contained: adequacy so defined is population-dependent by construction, though checked flat across n=1500/4000/8000.

anchor: N_viol is exact and bias-free
statement: N_viol, the count of conflicting Q-pairs within a representation fiber, is exact and bias-free (unlike the plug-in Hhat estimator with known small-sample bias) and is authoritative for the combinatorial question 'is adequacy exactly zero?'.

anchor: Data-Processing Inequality: for a deterministic sequential chain, H(Q|R5) <= H(Q|R4) <= H(Q|R3) <= H(Q|R2)
statement: The single [THM] in the entire Theory 00-14 register — the standard data-processing inequality, cited not re-derived, stated as the only theorem to make explicit how rare true theorem status is in this research programme.

anchor: a priori impossible ≠ empirically falsified
statement: A hypothesis (H-C, 'adequacy lost at step k and regained at k+j') was first recorded as 'refuted a priori', which was wrong; corrected to 'structurally inapplicable' to a sequential DPI-governed chain, distinguishing an ill-posed hypothesis from an empirically falsified one — recorded as the correction that matters, not pedantry.

anchor: The DPI applies to sequential families. It does not apply to a parallel family
statement: In a parallel family (every Rk=Tk(D) computed directly from D) non-monotone adequacy is perfectly possible; KR-BRIDGE-01/02/03 deliberately used a parallel family for exactly this reason.

anchor: Bytes are FLAT across R5→R3 while cardinality falls 8x. Fields never change.
statement: Reduction is genuinely multi-dimensional: measured bytes stayed at 37.0 from R5 to R4 while distinct-value cardinality fell from 26826 to 5696, refuting any single-scalar measure of 'how much was reduced'.

anchor: The bootstrap confidence interval on Ĥ is invalid in this design.
statement: Resampling with replacement duplicates cases, shrinking fiber diversity and depressing conditional entropy downward, biasing reported bootstrap CIs toward 'adequate'; contained because every adequacy verdict rests on the exact N_viol statistic and train/test splits, not the bootstrap CI.

anchor: OQ-1 — The carrier. blocks everything tactical
statement: KnowledgeOS has no declared mathematical carrier (every result on r=(value,source,tag,time), |D|<=6); closing it requires a governance decision informed by, not derived from, the experiments — no experiment can decide it.

anchor: DECISION-02: is φ a semantic evaluation frame or an evidence partition?
statement: Blocks the composition rule and the delta transition; experiments constrain but cannot decide it; also decides which bounded context owns phi.

anchor: OQ-4 — Adequacy vs Realization, actually exhibited
statement: Never achieved: requires a level with Hhat(Q|R)=0 and F<1 (a decoder deliberately weaker than the information, or a constraint that bites at an adequate level); flagged as the highest-value experiment available because it is the one separation the programme claims but has never shown.

anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
statement: Standing conjecture with an explicit refutation condition (one substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits); stated so it can be attacked rather than hardening into an assumption.

anchor: Do not promote any [EXP] to [THM]
statement: Explicit recommendation list of what NOT to do next: don't further tune the generator, don't widen the Pi x Q grid, don't declare a 'no-bridge law', don't promote [EXP] to [THM] (a theorem needs a proof not more evidence), don't move to a new algebra/Vedic-derived operator, don't test the Gita strand further for kernel candidacy, and don't open Theory v1.3 before adjudication.

anchor: The Gītā interpretive strand ran five cycles ... In none did it produce a kernel primitive

unknown_candidate.why_uncertain: closes out a five-cycle Gita-lens candidacy thread whose exact prior object identity is not independently confirmed from this file alone

statement: After five cycles (contradiction, elimination, reduction, audit, bridge) the Gita lens has never been the source of a result; recommendation to keep it external and stop testing it for kernel candidacy — its role is naming what an experiment already earned.

anchor: Theory v1.2 remains FROZEN. The kernel remains NOT SELECTED. No algebra is declared. No carrier is declared.
statement: The standing position closing the Theory 00-14 set: nothing in the thirteen/fifteen-document set is adjudicated; the set exists so that adjudication is now possible.

anchor: KnowledgeOS requires four-valued logic is NOT supported.
statement: Tested contradiction requirements do not force a fourth flat value; flat candidates A/B/C fail the same seven required distinctions, whose common failure lies in the unknown/boundary family, not contradiction itself — reframing 'the problem that looked like a contradiction problem' as a boundary/unknown problem.

anchor: A structured reason/boundary component is indispensable within the tested candidate representation language.
statement: Wording explicitly softened by measurement, not rewording, from an earlier overclaim that 'reason is the sole indispensable field'; reason-expressivity objection is tested and answered (reason takes 10 values and the finding survives factorization).

anchor: Minimum flat cardinality depends on the declared required-distinction set.
statement: There is no context-free answer to 'how many truth values do we need'; the structural requirement grew the state space from chi=3 to chi=21 but the finding is that cardinality is the wrong axis, not that 21 values are needed.

anchor: The commissioned witness shape does not separate the three [composition] rules. A different shape does — and the commissioned shape eliminates a rule outright instead.
statement: W1 (commissioned witness) eliminates last-wins via a C1 failure on all six surviving triples instead of separating the three rules; W2 (an alternate witness with no internal conflict) separates majority from intraframe-only; C6 order-invariance eliminates last-wins a second time independently — the separating witness must have no internal conflict.

anchor: last-wins is not well-defined on the evidence set — its output depends on enumeration order.
statement: A composition rule must be a function of the evidence set, not of its listing; last-wins is eliminated twice, independently (by W1's C1 failure and by C6 order-invariance).

anchor: K_t → A_t (AttributedState). Knows → True is external and factive; Verification is a separate concern
statement: DECIDED under factivity work (R1): an earlier evaluator returned T for uninterpreted/theory-incomplete states, a defect unfair to the competing candidate; the strengthened evaluator carries an explicit evaluator_exists flag.

anchor: The rank-convention result is NOT a further instance [of DECISION-01].
statement: DECISION-01 ('semantic evaluation must be invariant under non-evidential variation') is RATIFIED, but the rank-convention reading required an invertible recoding that the audit refuted with 21369 tie violations; the claim was withdrawn by both the original author and the review's replacement wording.

anchor: DECISION-02 — Is φ a semantic evaluation frame, or an evidence partition? OPEN, and blocking
statement: The single largest open governance item in the contradiction/composition lane: nothing downstream may be settled by inference from experiments, which only constrain, not decide, it.

anchor: Pairwise semantic/evidential distinguishability cannot carry family-level epistemic complexity by itself.
statement: FR-001, FROZEN 2026-09-02 as a research-result freeze (not a theory/architecture decision), established by two independent failure mechanisms: sim_Lambda is not transitive (sorites witness spanning 3.068 at delta=0.3099) and the transitivity-free delta-packing repair captures redundancy but fails on coupling (correlated up to 222x); KR-HILBERT's spectral route strengthened rather than reopened the freeze.

anchor: reason is the sole indispensable field
statement: FR-002 explicitly withheld from freezing (CANDIDATE, NOT FROZEN) pending re-check of this exact wording, since softened and tested by measurement; the candidate list stands but the freeze does not.

anchor: Read-disjointness must be discharged on the triple (Π, Q, T) and verified empirically.
statement: FR-003, CANDIDATE this cycle, established by KR-BRIDGE-02 §2 catching a false positive (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) that a hand-inspected provenance map (wrong twice) would otherwise have let through; needs a second independent adopter before promotion per ES-006.1.

anchor: individual Zero ⟹ group Zero [and converse] ... [NEG] (both directions)
statement: The refutation ledger of Zero-algebra claims: L is not a projection, L is not confluent, individual<=>group Zero fails both directions (131 and 63 violations), Z is not down/up/union/intersection-closed as a standard regime, Z is not a matroid, Z is not generated by its minimal elements, and relational transformations are not necessary for higher-order Zero.

anchor: Zero predicts preservation [NEG] — 4 independent tests
statement: Refuted claims about the bridge: Zero does not predict preservation (4 independent tests), Zero does not mark the reduction boundary, admissibility is a property of (Pi,Q,T) not (Pi,Q), read-disjointness cannot be established by declaration, and neither flattening the redundancy distribution nor raising population size increases informative strata.

anchor: Claims withdrawn by their author, which is a separate category
statement: A distinct register from refutation-by-opponent: five self-withdrawn claims are listed (an unproven ordering claim, the KR-BRIDGE-01 single-mechanism explanation superseded by two causes at r=2, a 'representation class is flat' claim overturned by a generator defect where 40.2% of cases bypassed mk(), the section-5 rank headline refuted by audit FAIL 2.3, and 'H-C refuted a priori' corrected to structurally inapplicable), kept visible so retraction is not quietly forgotten.

anchor: The strongest statement made must never exceed the strength of the available evidence.
statement: The rule this whole frozen/refuted register document enforces, with its operational form: keep facts, architectural conclusions, governance decisions, engineering actions and operational observations rigorously separate — never let one silently become another.

anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
statement: KR-BRIDGE-01 (Outcome A): a large marginal association (pooled RD=-0.363) dissolved under stratification, explained by redundancy as a confounder within one informative stratum/carrier/Pi/Q/transformation; tightened on review to forbid stating it as a general causal law.

anchor: The one substantial effect in the entire grid was an artifact of shared reads.
statement: KR-BRIDGE-02's instrument failed twice before reporting anything: first a marginal-RD adjudication falsely reported 'H2 SUPPORTED, 27/27 replicate' (re-finding the known confounder), then a naive read-disjointness gate let through an inadmissible cell (MH-RD=-0.155, replicating) caused by rank=f(value,tag) leaking into Pi; a second, corrected gate was itself found unsound by perturbation testing (Pi_arity effectively reading value via dedup survivorship), yielding the rule 'admissibility is a property of the TRIPLE (Pi,Q,T), never of the pair' and 'declaration is not verification.'

anchor: CELLS ACTUALLY SEARCHED: 31 of 112
statement: Final KR-BRIDGE-02 tally: 112 cells, 14 excluded by gate, 67 with no informative stratum, 15 with RD_within=0, 2 non-replicating, 14 survivors of which 0 were substantive on both splits, 1 borderline, 13 negligible; H1 not refuted, with 12 of 14 survivors having no stratum whose 95% CI excluded zero.

anchor: Flattening the redundancy distribution does not increase informative strata
statement: KR-BRIDGE-03 found flattening the redundancy distribution moved informative strata only 73->75 because flattening moves mass into deterministic extremes (r=0: Zero never fires; r=3: Zero always fires) that cannot be informative by construction; the effective lever instead is record count (73->233 at n_rec 4->6), while population size is not a lever (73/74/70 at n=1500/4000/8000).

anchor: 67 dead cells, in every one of the nine regimes. The count did not move by one.
statement: Cause identified as adequacy saturation (most (T,Q) pairs fully preserve or fully destroy Q, 25-31 of 35 combinations sitting at 0.00 or 1.00), a property of the adequacy definition rather than the generator, evidenced across nine regimes; the remaining lever is (T,Q) designs that partially preserve each Q.

anchor: No Zero/preservation bridge exists for read-disjoint (Π, Q).
statement: Standing conjecture stated with an explicit refutation condition (a single substantive, replicating, gate-clean cell with |MH-RD|>=0.01 on both splits, gate passed, stratum CI excluding zero); explicitly not a law given one carrier family and 31 of 112 cells searched.

anchor: Zero is contract-relative. ... Zero is reference-relative.
statement: KR-ZERO-ALGEBRA H8: 495 of 4049 tested pairs change their Zero verdict under a contract-detail change; H7: 541 of 4260 differ under a reference change — eliminability is not intrinsic to the data.

anchor: L is not a projection. The tested algebra is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process.
statement: Across H1-H11: idempotence is operator-relative (PARTIAL), commutativity fails (11/1162 non-commuting), termination and monotone-decreasing iteration hold, individual<=>group Zero fails both directions (131 and 63 violations), reference/contract invariance fail (541/4260, 495/4049), invariant != Zero (1865 vs 858 mismatches), Remainder=D-Eliminated fails for the transformation residual (equality only 816/1182), and RuleEliminable != CounterfactualZero (55.75% agreement) — which normal form you halt at depends on elimination order.

anchor: Z is NOT generated upward by its minimal elements — 286 / 826 failures
statement: Set-structure closure properties of Zero-subsets Z mostly fail (downward-closed, upward-closed, union-closed all refuted; intersection-closed refuted by only 2 cases and fits exactly once a cancelling contract is removed; not a matroid); the practical consequence is there is no compact generator-based encoding of eliminability — caching minimal eliminable sets and expanding them upward will be wrong.

anchor: "Not eliminated" IS exactly "contract-relevant unresolved material" — a genuine and non-obvious identity, holding without exception in the tested space.
statement: The positive result inside the refuted H10: of three candidate 'Remainder' constructions (D-Eliminated, transformation residual, contract-unresolved material), A and C agree exactly in 1182/1182 tested cases while B (the transformation residual) is a different object agreeing with the others only 816/1182 times — 'the residue of the operation is not the residue of the concern.'

anchor: the eliminability ladder reaches at least k = 3
statement: Demonstrated empirically for n<=6 that some sets are eliminable only as a triple, not pairwise; k>3 is explicitly OPEN and n<=6 is a design bound, not a property of eliminability; the phenomenon is transformation-specific (T2_dedup 28.2% higher-order rate vs T7 exactly 0%), and relational transformations are shown to produce but not be necessary for higher-order Zero.

anchor: One elimination in six is prevented by boundary information alone
statement: Direct empirical support (provenance, uncertainty, scope, contradiction state) for treating boundary/provenance as load-bearing rather than metadata, described as the strongest link from the Zero lane to the kernel design.

anchor: The estimand for any bridge claim is the within-stratum effect.
statement: The programme's central methodological error was estimating the wrong quantity competently — the marginal P(A|Z)-P(A|not Z) was already known to be confounded before KR-BRIDGE-02 ran; re-estimating it produced a false 'H2 SUPPORTED'; the correct estimand is the Mantel-Haenszel within-stratum effect.

anchor: A stratum is informative iff (a_k+b_k)>0 ∧ (c_k+d_k)>0 ∧ (a_k+c_k)>0 ∧ (b_k+d_k)>0
statement: Both Zero and non-Zero must occur and both Adequate and Inadequate must occur for a stratum to be informative; strata at deterministic extremes contribute nothing, explaining why flattening the redundancy distribution failed (balance is not power) and why choosing a finer stratification variable (multiplicity partition, then partition x |S|) gave 13x the informative strata.

anchor: Sign agreement alone is not replication.
statement: Under a sign-only replication rule, 14 cells 'replicated' with |RD|~0.001 and 12 of 14 had no stratum CI excluding zero; all 14 collapsed at higher power. Replication requires sign agreement AND clearing a substantive floor on both splits AND at least one stratum's 95% CI excluding zero; per-stratum RDs must be reported, not only the pooled MH estimate.

anchor: If the floor is declared after first inspection, record that fact in the artifact
statement: Effect-size floors must be declared and used as a reporting tier rather than a filter (publish every surviving cell at both tiers) since at n~10^5 statistical significance is not evidence of anything; a post-inspection floor must be disclosed as such.

anchor: Bootstrap CI on Ĥ ... [DEFECT] invalid here
statement: Estimator hygiene register: N_viol is exact and bias-free (authoritative for combinatorial adequacy questions), the Miller-Madow correction is used for Hhat, Haldane+0.5/Woolf CI is used for sparse odds-ratio tables, and bootstrap CI on Hhat is invalid because resampling duplicates cases and depresses conditional entropy.

anchor: Within the tested deduplication regime, redundancy behaves as a common cause of Zero occurrence and of inadequacy.
statement: Standard formalized here: never state a regime-specific empirical finding as a general causal law; a single-mechanism explanation of the KR-BRIDGE-01 confound was itself withdrawn once the Zero-count was found constant at r=1 but varying at r=2, showing the exact RD=0 had two different causes.

anchor: Power is a property of the informative region, not of n.
statement: Measured across four candidate power levers: population size (no effect, 73/74/70 across n=1500/4000/8000) and flattening the confounder distribution (73->75, no effect) both do nothing, while record count (73->233) and finer stratification variable (~30->388) are the effective levers; when power stops responding to sampling, the constraint has moved into the design (the 67 dead cells are invariant across nine generator regimes because the adequacy definition itself saturates).

anchor: labels are pre-registered classifications, not established facts.
statement: Amendment A1, originating from KR-BRIDGE-01's T_B label mismatch: after execution a pre-registered label (e.g. 'lossy') is verified against observed behaviour and a mismatch is a recorded finding, never silently redefined to match its label.

anchor: do not tune the generator to balance cells. Natural imbalance is evidence.
statement: Amendment A2: cells are reported with their structural cause, never engineered, because balancing an imbalanced four-way table would destroy the information that the imbalance itself was the finding.

anchor: Control A1 is the one that earned its place this cycle.
statement: A ten-control checklist (preserving/destroying/invertible-recoding/four-way-non-degeneracy/separation/Zero-fires-selectively/gate-bites/Pi-not-inert/Q-not-inert/provenance-verified-by-perturbation); Control A1 (perturbation-verified provenance) caught two hand-written provenance maps that were wrong, which code review had not caught.

anchor: Distinguish structurally inapplicable from empirically refuted
statement: Originating from hypothesis H-C being wrongly recorded as 'refuted' when it was actually ill-posed against a sequential DPI-governed design; crediting the experiment with a result it could not have produced would be a false result in the negative direction.

anchor: the check discriminates; it does not merely dissolve.
statement: The generalized provenance check both dissolved the KR-ZERO-GROUP 'case J' finding (revealed as a property of cancelling contracts, not of Zero) and confirmed/strengthened the interaction-order finding (which came out higher without the cancelling contract) — the contrast is evidence the check is a real instrument, not a way to disbelieve inconvenient results.

anchor: Hypothesis → Estimand → O-F* → Population → Calibration → Control → Freeze → Execution → Adjudication
statement: The experimental protocol frozen 2026-09-05, introducing O-F* (Estimand Non-Degeneracy Preflight): every declared-variable quantity must have a pre-execution variation witness under the frozen computation because 'class reachability does not imply estimand variability'; it runs before the freeze because its failure is grounds to rewrite the estimand while that is still legitimate.

anchor: Observed diagnostic ⇏ new primary estimand ... Observed convergence ⇏ theory promotion
statement: Two research-governance safeguards (explicitly not theory claims) stated because KR-ZOOM-03's directed diagnostic and KR-ZOOM-OUT-01's conditional-population result both appeared only after the pre-registered primary estimand had already returned a weaker verdict and could not be adopted; calibration must be a separate pass with its own gate, inspected before analysis code runs, because in KR-ZOOM-OUT-01 the null stratum silently became the 'winning' M1 artifact and the calibration-gate failure was invisible until audit.

anchor: Engineering supplies evidence and never accepts its own work
statement: The governance order EXPERIMENT -> AUDIT -> ADJUDICATION -> THEORY v1.3 is stated as part of the method itself, with no shortcuts: evidence, recommendation, and authority stay separate.

anchor: Restriction changes the information boundary. Inquiry changes the investigative focus while retaining the information boundary.
statement: A conceptual correction required before further zoom experiments could be meaningful: KR-ZOOM-01 implemented restriction and reported it as zoom, producing three 'defects' that were actually one defect; restriction and inquiry are not two readings of one operator.

anchor: Observe → Focus → Explore → Assess → Determine → Update
statement: The corrected research model replacing a representation-reduction reading of the zoom cycle: Focus(K_t,O_i) does not destroy K_t, and Investigate(Q_i) may discover dimensions not present in the initial focus; contrasted explicitly with D -> D\S restriction/elimination, which belongs to the Zero lane not here.

anchor: 13x the effort bought exactly nothing
statement: P3 (restrictive boundaries impose an epistemic ceiling), described as the strongest result in the zoom lane: restriction stays flat at 0.079/0.071 from probe budget 3 to 40 while inquiry rises from 0.511 to 1.000, and paired_restriction_only=0.000 at every budget across 8000 cases — restricting the view never once helped.

anchor: Inquiry focus should be substantially order-robust under a fixed inquiry and evidence environment.
statement: A fourth candidate principle (order robustness): restriction/descent shows 0.000 internal-state agreement under exploration-order swap (0/518) vs ~0.92 for inquiry/focus; stated as a conjecture with a refutation condition, noting a persistent 3-8% 'different state, same observable' residual cell as the corpus's third independent occurrence of that phenomenon.

anchor: context_preserved = 1.000 must never be written as 'the experiment demonstrated perfect context preservation.'
statement: A definitional-vs-evidential distinction: several measured 1.000/0.000 quantities (context preservation, restriction's inability to find cross-dimension causes, the 0.87525 'Zero before evidence' rate that is identical to the generator's cross-dimension rate relabelled) are forced by design and must be reported as such, not as empirical results — now a standing methodological rule referenced to the epistemic-status vocabulary.

anchor: FR-004 CANDIDATE — Determination is relational, not intrinsic: Determine = Determine(K, Q, C, E_C, S, R)
statement: Raised by the research owner 2026-09-05 as a candidate methodological invariant, explicitly not promoted: determination is not an intrinsic property of K — changing the epistemic standard S (margin, uniqueness rule) changes the determined-case set with no change to K; the same relational shape appears convergently in six places (inquiry-relative adequacy, Zero's contract/reference-relativity, epistemic standards, reasoning-regime-dependent composition, set-valued determination, and the Zoom-out M0/M1 split), making it a strong design principle but not a theorem since experimental convergence is not proof.

anchor: Reachability ≠ Determination ≠ Knowledge
statement: Measured via KR-ZOOM-OUT-02-SELECTION-AUDIT: every root was reachable within budget (P_reach=P_all) yet P(Determine|Reach) was only 0.367/0.368 — 63% of cases were fully reachable and still not determined, because determination failed at the contract level (uniqueness/margin conditions), not the search level; a third instance of a recurring separation alongside Information!=Evidence and Evidence!=Determination.

anchor: Zoom-in as inquiry/focus operation — Supported candidate, operationally usable ... Zoom-out definition — [OPEN] — UNDEFINED
statement: Standing position adjudicated 2026-09-05: the zoom method is validated enough to use Zoom-in/Zoom-out as engineering/investigation operations but has not proved a universal epistemological definition of either; Zoom-in is usable now as a candidate operational pattern (never a kernel primitive), while Zoom-out remains undefined — the KR-ZOOM-OUT-01/02/03 experiments produced negative/methodological output (the M1 artifact, the FR-004 prediction failure, O-F* itself) rather than a definition of Zoom-out; ZoomIn != ZoomOut != RepresentationReduction is named the durable contribution of the zoom lane so far.

anchor: Every future mathematical statement in KnowledgeOS must carry its epistemic status: Definition, Theorem, Corollary, Empirical Result, Proposition, Conjecture, Refuted, or Open.
statement: Adopted 2026-09-04 for the KnowledgeOS research lane, issued by the human research owner as a permanent methodological rule; an untagged mathematical statement is declared a defect — the exact mechanism by which an experiment becomes a theorem without anyone deciding that it should.

anchor: This EXTENDS the existing vocabulary — it does not replace it (ES-005.4, never a copy)
statement: The zero-algebra lane already used [EXP]/[OPEN]/[NEG]/[DEF] (plus [PROP]/[THEORY]/[DESIGN]/[DEFECT]); five of eight required categories already existed, so [THM] (theorem, proof cited/contained), [COR] (corollary, cited antecedent + stated derivation), and [CONJ] (conjecture, must state its refutation condition) are added as genuinely new tags rather than duplicating the vocabulary.

anchor: [PROP] is ambiguous and is retired as a live tag
statement: [PROP] collided between 'proposal/recommendation' (KR-BRIDGE-02's usage) and the mathematical sense 'proposition' (a proved statement of lesser weight than a theorem); resolved per the repository's existing legacy-alias pattern (EXPERIMENT-ID-REGISTRY) into [PRP] (Proposition, proved, live) and [REC] (Recommendation, no truth claim, live), with [PROP] retired as a legacy alias only; every existing [PROP] use in the zero-algebra results is confirmed to be the recommendation sense, none a proved proposition.

anchor: [EXP] NEVER becomes [THM] by accumulating experiments. A theorem needs a PROOF.

statement: Theorems 24.1 (Zero Equivalence) and 25.1 (Gap Reduction) are proved, with an explicit limitation that gap comparison across differing contracts (EC_t != EC_{t+1}) requires an explicit compatibility mapping — 'moving the goalposts' is formally blocked by the Contract Compatibility principle GapComparison=>ContractCompatibility.

anchor: V(K_t) ⊆ V(K_{t+1}) ∧ H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) ... Historical existence ≠ Current epistemic standing.
statement: Axiom A6 (Historical Preservation) plus the constitutional distinction between historical existence and current epistemic standing: a proposition can move Supported->Retracted without deleting the historical fact that it was once asserted and supported; replaces 'universal epistemic monotonicity' with this weaker, correct invariant.

anchor: Truth ≠ Evaluation ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
statement: Axiom A2 (Epistemic Pipeline Separation), with the worked consequence that EVal(p)=Supported does not mean Decision=Permit (a governance policy may instead require HumanReview) — epistemic status is explicitly not equivalent to operational authorization.

anchor: Contr(p) ⇏ ∀q ∈ 𝒫, q. ... Local contradiction ⇏ Global epistemic collapse.
statement: Axiom A5 (Non-Explosion): KnowledgeOS explicitly rejects the classical explosion principle as a system rule, requiring contradiction to be scoped and represented rather than collapsing all propositions.

anchor: 𝒪_core = {ASSERT, LINK, REVISE, RETRACT, ISOLATE}
statement: Names the frozen candidate core operation interface (introduce an assertion, establish a relation, change content while preserving history, withdraw standing without erasing history, and restrict propagation of a contradiction or dangerous structure), with full preconditions/postconditions/composition laws deferred to later parts.

anchor: ABK-1 is a validated candidate-adequate architecture for the target problem class.
statement: Explicitly withdraws the earlier claim that ABK-1 is 'the universally unique minimal KnowledgeOS kernel' as circular, replacing it with the weaker, defensible claim that global minimality remains unproven unless the candidate representation space and equivalence relation are formally characterized.

anchor: Ontology defines what kinds of things KnowledgeOS reasons about. Representation defines how those things are encoded.
statement: States the ontology/representation boundary underlying Part II's many-sorted type system (Ent, Val, Attr, Dim, Prop, Asrt, Obs, Evd, Src, Rel, Evt, St, Ctx, Part, Prov, ES, Req, Inq, EC, Pol, Dec, Act), asserting a database/graph/JSON/RDF/object-model representation is never the ontology itself.

anchor: Let D be a value domain and n:D→ℝ a numerical encoding. If no semantic operation corresponding to subtraction is defined on D, then n(x)−n(y) cannot ... be interpreted as a valid semantic difference.
statement: Theorem 2.1 (Representation does not imply arithmetic validity), with proof, establishing that numerical computability of a difference does not by itself establish semantic validity of that difference.

anchor: Supports(e,p) ⇏ Truth(p).
statement: Proposition 2.1, proved by the type-mismatch argument that support is an epistemic evidence-proposition relation while truth is a semantic proposition-model relation with different domains and meanings; called one of the most important anti-confusion principles in KnowledgeOS.

anchor: Let R:𝕂→X be a representation function. Suppose there exist K1≠K2 such that R(K1)=R(K2). If there exists an inquiry Q such that Answer(Q,K1,Γ)≠Answer(Q,K2,Γ), then R is inadequate for Q,Γ.
statement: Theorem 2.3 (Semantically lossy representation), with proof, generalizing Part I's Theorem 16.1 to the knowledge-state level and formally establishing why representation adequacy must be question-relative.

anchor: Status_Γ,EC(p)=σ ... We deliberately do not define one universal ordered list such as Unknown<Supported<Proven<Rejected.
statement: Epistemic Status is defined as contract- and context-dependent rather than a single universal total order, giving formal meaning to 'unknown' as neither true nor false rather than as a weaker degree of falsity.

anchor: If Conflict is represented as a local relation on propositions, then the existence of a conflict concerning p does not by itself entail conflict concerning arbitrary q.
statement: Theorem 2.5 (Locality theorem for contradiction), with proof, giving the formal ontological grounding for the non-explosion axiom stated in Part I.

anchor: KnowledgeOS SHALL NOT treat stored data as knowledge merely because it is stored.
statement: Ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) close Part II — proposition/evidence separation, observation/proposition separation, decision/action separation, epistemic-status/truth separation, identity/state separation, evidence/truth separation, contract relativity, historical preservation, non-explosion, and representation independence — as the boundaries preventing KnowledgeOS from collapsing into an ordinary information system.

anchor: Truth → Evidence → Evaluation → Determination → Decision ... The arrows indicate dependency possibilities, not logical equivalence.
statement: Defines five explicit semantic layers (Truth_M(p), Evid(e,p), Eval(K,p,Gamma), Det(K,p,EC,Gamma), Dec(K,Q,P,A,Gamma)) to prevent classical truth, evidence, uncertainty, contradiction and operational determination from being silently collapsed into one binary logic with metadata.

anchor: Assumed(a) ... a ∧ b ⇒ p ... Knowledge(p∣A) ⇏ Knowledge(p)
statement: Formalizes conditional/assumption-dependent knowledge, requiring KnowledgeOS to distinguish p from p|A and forbidding silent unconditional promotion of a conditional conclusion, modeling justification itself as an inspectable directed graph (Supports/Challenges/DerivedFrom/Assumes/Defeats edges) rather than a scalar status label — named a DDD consequence: justification should be a domain concept, not logging metadata.

anchor: Unknown ≠ Ambiguous ≠ Uncertain ≠ Conflicted
statement: Four uncertainty concepts are formally separated (unavailable information / multiple compatible interpretations / probability-model-assigned uncertainty / incompatible coexisting claims) and must not collapse into one generic false/null/low-confidence value.

anchor: No numerical probability may be introduced without an explicitly defined probability model. ... Confidence=0.8 cannot be treated as a universal epistemic quantity.
statement: A strict statistical discipline requiring a full probability space (Omega,F,P) before any numeric probability statement is meaningful; likewise 'no estimator is meaningful without a declared estimand', preserving Estimand != Estimator != Estimate.

anchor: Distinct Evidence Records ≠ Independent Evidence
statement: Statistical independence must never be inferred merely from organizational or textual record separation (two reports may independently quote the same original source); a contract requiring independent corroboration must define independence explicitly.

anchor: No valid KnowledgeOS implementation may infer, solely from an epistemic status s, s⇒Truth(p), unless the applicable epistemic contract explicitly provides and satisfies a soundness bridge.
statement: Theorem 3.3 (Epistemic non-collapse), with proof, the culminating invariant of Part III; only an explicit, separately proved soundness bridge can license Det=>Truth.

anchor: Evidence Context ... Epistemic Evaluation Context ... Determination Context ... Decision Context
statement: Proposes four candidate (not yet ratified) bounded contexts derived from the epistemic pipeline's semantic layering, plus an anti-corruption-layer example: an external 'status=APPROVED' field must not be automatically interpreted as Determined(p) without an explicit declared mapping (undeclared cases default to Unknown).

anchor: K ≠ set of currently accepted propositions. ... K = CurrentEpistemicState + HistoricalContext + Justification + Provenance + Governance.
statement: Rejects a naive knowledge-state model K={p1,...,pn} because two systems can share the same current propositions while differing in provenance, justification, evidence, and history; K = <Current(K), History(K)>.

anchor: ASSERT(a) ⇏ Established(a). ... RETRACT ≠ DELETE. ... ISOLATE is not rejection.
statement: Formally defines the five core operations (ASSERT introduces without accepting; LINK creates a typed relation without asserting external validity; REVISE changes current interpretation while preserving H(K_t)⊆H(K_{t+1}); RETRACT withdraws current standing while preserving historical existence, explicitly not deletion; ISOLATE separates incompatible interpretations without rejecting either), each with formal preconditions.

anchor: δ: 𝕂×𝒪×Ctx → 𝕂∪{⊥} ... Rejected operation ≠ successful state transition.
statement: Defines the transition function with an explicit invalid-transition symbol bottom, and states that a rejected operation may still be recorded historically (RejectedEvent(o,reason,t)) distinct from an accepted transition.

anchor: Suppose Valid(K_t,Γ_t) and Pre(o_t,K_t,Γ_t) and δ is a valid KnowledgeOS transition function. Then Valid(K_{t+1},Γ_{t+1}) ...
statement: Theorem 4.1 (Valid-state preservation) and Theorem 4.2 (history preservation H_t⊆H_{t+1}), both proved, plus the corollary that history preservation does NOT imply K_t⊆K_{t+1} in general (a status can move Established->Retracted) — the system is historically monotonic but epistemically non-monotonic.

anchor: δ(δ(K,o1,Γ),o2,Γ) need not equal δ(δ(K,o2,Γ),o1,Γ). ... An operation o is idempotent if δ(δ(K,o,Γ),o,Γ)=δ(K,o,Γ).
statement: Establishes operations are generally non-commutative (worked example: ASSERT then RETRACT is meaningful, the reverse order may be invalid or different) and that idempotence must be verified per operation rather than assumed universally (LINK may be idempotent; duplicate ASSERT is not, in general, because assertion identity can depend on provenance/time/context).

anchor: If: 1. the initial state K0 is fixed; 2. δ is deterministic; 3. every transition input is preserved; 4. all rule versions and required contexts are preserved; then replaying the historical sequence reconstructs the same semantic state.
statement: Theorem 4.3 (Reproducibility), proved by induction on t, establishing formally why provenance, rule versioning, and context preservation are not optional audit decoration but load-bearing for reproducibility.

anchor: KnowledgeOS does not define completeness as possession of all possible information. It defines completeness as satisfaction of a specified requirement set under a specified epistemic contract.
statement: States the central principle of Part V's gap algebra, built on EC->Req->Sat->Delta->Zero.

anchor: Δ_1 ⊆ Δ_2 ... Two gaps may be incomparable ... there is no mathematically justified statement that one is universally 'more complete' merely from these sets.
statement: Defines gap containment as a partial (not total) order, giving a worked counterexample (Delta1={r1,r2}, Delta2={r2,r3}) where neither gap contains the other.

anchor: It is tempting to assume Δ_{t+1} ⊆ Δ_t. That is not universally valid. ... Discovering a previously hidden gap can improve epistemic quality even when explicit gap cardinality increases.
statement: Explicitly corrects the tempting assumption of monotone gap reduction: revision, retraction, conflict discovery, or changed evidence/authority/temporal validity can legitimately produce Delta_{t+1}⊃Delta_t; a larger explicit gap can represent better epistemic awareness than a false Delta=0, formalized via a distinction between Delta^known and Delta^true.

anchor: For a fixed requirement universe I: 𝒢(I)=𝒫(I) ... Zero ⟺ Δ=⊥_G.
statement: Establishes that, for a fixed requirement universe, gaps form a Boolean/power-set lattice under set inclusion with meet=intersection, join=union, bottom=empty set (=Zero) and top=I; explicitly flags this algebra as contract-bound (I=Req(EC,Gamma)) and warns that the gap lattice is not automatically an ordering of the whole knowledge-state space.

anchor: FalseZero ⟺ ZeroClaim ∧ Δ≠∅ ... A KnowledgeOS governance system should therefore treat Zero claims as auditable assertions rather than ordinary status fields.
statement: Defines a 'False Zero' governance failure mode (claiming completeness while the gap is non-empty) as more serious than an ordinary missing requirement because it suppresses representation of the gap itself, requiring a reconstructible Trace_Zero (contract, requirements, satisfaction, evidence, rules, versions, context, time, authority).

anchor: Suppose ... every requirement in Req(EC,Γ) is stable under the allowed transition; ... Then Δ(K_{t+1},EC,Γ)=∅. Therefore Zero(K_t,EC,Γ) ⇒ Zero(K_{t+1},EC,Γ).
statement: Theorem 5.2 (Conditional Zero Preservation), proved under four explicit stability assumptions; without them Zero preservation does not follow, and the strongest universally defensible claim is only 'KnowledgeOS can establish contractual Zero relative to a declared requirement universe, context, rule set, and epistemic state' — never absolute or permanent Zero.

anchor: Evidence → Evaluation → Satisfaction → Determination ... with decision deliberately remaining outside this chain
statement: States the core determination-calculus chain and formally separates Evidence, Evaluation, Determination and Decision as four distinct semantic categories.

anchor: EvidenceCount ≠ EvidenceStrength. ... Strength(E) = Σ_i Strength(e_i) [is] not generally valid.
statement: Rejects additive evidence aggregation as a default (evidence may be redundant, dependent, contradictory, differently reliable/relevant, or based on the same underlying observation); requires an explicit aggregation model rather than assumed addition.

anchor: Det(K,p,EC,Γ) ⟺ ∀r ∈ Req_p(EC,Γ), χ_EC(Sat(K,r,Γ))=1. ... Det(K,p,EC,Γ) ⟺ Δ_p(K,EC,Γ)=∅.
statement: Definition 6.2 and Theorem 6.1 (Determination-Gap Equivalence, proved) give the proposition-level analogue of Part V's global Zero, plus Theorem 6.2 (Requirement-Complete Determination) and a further conditional Sound Determination Theorem requiring five explicit soundness assumptions before Det=>Truth_M(p) may be asserted.

anchor: Type I — Evidence error ... Type VI — Governance error
statement: Distinguishes six materially different epistemic failure modes (evidence, evaluation, inference, contract, representation, governance error), warning that a single generic 'KnowledgeError' loses important domain information.

anchor: Determination = ⟨Target,Contract,Context,Evidence,Rules,Assumptions,Result,Authority,Time,Provenance⟩. The Boolean outcome is a projection.
statement: Argues determination is an epistemic act with a full structural record, not a Boolean field (determined=true), with candidate lifecycle Proposed->Evaluating->Determined->Challenged->Revised->Retracted; likewise proposes evidence and evaluation should be first-class domain concepts/services, not reduced to Document or DatabaseRecord.

anchor: Dep(r_i,r_j) ⇏ ¬Sat(r_j) without a declared dependency rule. ... Affected(e) ... and its transitive dependents.
statement: Formalizes requirement-to-evidence traceability and reverse traceability (a newly invalidated evidence item identifies every requirement/determination potentially affected) as the mathematical basis for impact analysis and scoped, minimal re-evaluation.

anchor: Current Epistemic State ≠ Epistemic History. ... H_t ⊆ H_{t+1}.
statement: Central principle of Part VII: a KnowledgeOS state must be able to say simultaneously 'this was previously determined' and 'it is no longer currently determined' without contradiction, because they refer to different temporal states; Definition 7.1 formalizes historical preservation as H(K_t)⊆H(K_{t+1}).

anchor: DataGrowth ⇏ KnowledgeMonotonicity.
statement: Worked example: a database gaining a contradictory observation about p can cause the current determination to move from Established to Conflicted even though Records_t⊆Records_{t+1} — monotonic data growth does not imply monotonic knowledge consequence.

anchor: REVISE ≠ Deletion. ... Retracted(p) ⇏ False(p).
statement: Definitions 7.2/7.3 (Revision, Retraction): revision changes current status while preserving H(K)⊆H(K'); retraction withdraws current epistemic support (CurrentStatus=Retracted) without implying Delete(p) or False(p) — a proposition can be retracted for reasons (unreliable evidence, invalid provenance, changed contract, unsound rule, failed dependency) unrelated to its truth.

anchor: H(K_t) ⊆ H(K_{t+1}) for every valid transition ... Corollary: Retraction Does Not Destroy History.
statement: Theorem 7.76 (Revision Theorem — Historical Preservation) with proof and its corollary, reaffirming Part IV's history-preservation result specifically for the revision/retraction operations covered in this Part.

anchor: Event Time, Knowledge Time, Valid Time, Transaction Time
statement: Introduces bitemporal/multi-temporal semantics (event time vs knowledge time vs valid time vs transaction time) as the temporal vocabulary this Part uses to describe when a revision or retraction is recorded versus when the underlying event occurred.

anchor: Knowledge evolution is not necessarily gap monotonic.
statement: Closing constitutional summary: Delta_{t+1} can strictly exceed Delta_t under revision; conflict is represented without logical explosion (p, not p not-entails q); competing interpretations may be isolated as K^(1)...K^(n); revision must preserve HistoricalStanding != CurrentStanding.

anchor: = structural equality, ≡_sem semantic equivalence, ≈_{Q,Γ} observational equivalence relative to an inquiry and context, and ≅_prov provenance-sensitive equivalence.
statement: Four identity/equivalence relations are formally separated and required never to collapse into one universal notion of 'same'; adds a fifth, equiv_EC (contract-relative equivalence), later in the part.

anchor: Same semantic object ≠ same record ... Same record ≠ same epistemic meaning
statement: States the identity/representation boundary motivating the whole Part: identity must be defined per semantic type rather than assumed universal (proposition identity, assertion identity, and observation identity are each treated separately).

anchor: Proposition identity does not imply assertion identity
statement: Two assertions of the same proposition from different sources/times are distinct epistemic events; collapsing them merely because they share a proposition could falsely manufacture 'multiple independent sources confirm a claim' from what is really one proposition asserted twice.

anchor: Structural identity, semantic equivalence, observational equivalence, and provenance-sensitive equivalence SHALL remain distinct concepts. ... Preserve every distinction that the contract requires; collapse only what the contract permits.
statement: Eighteen constitutional statements (VIII-C1..VIII-C18) close the Part, covering identity-type-specificity, assertion/observation/evidence preservation, provenance preservation, representation independence, contract-relative adequacy, prohibitions on silent semantic collapse or false splitting, deduplication governance, temporal/revision/replay identity, and the closing principle that same-representation/meaning/provenance/observation/epistemic-role are all mutually distinct.

anchor: Relation ≠ Inference ... Correlation ≠ Causation ... Graph connectivity ≠ semantic dependency
statement: States the three boundaries governing Part IX: a graph is a representation of typed semantic relations, not itself a theory of knowledge.

anchor: r = ⟨type, source, target, context, time, provenance, status⟩ ... Supports:ℰ×𝒫→𝔹
statement: Defines relations as typed, provenance-bearing first-class semantic objects with declared signatures (Supports, Contradicts, Describes, DependsOn, DerivedFrom, Supersedes, Causes), rejecting untyped generic graph edges.

anchor: Path ≠ Inference ... MultiplePaths ≠ IndependentEvidence
statement: Warns that graph connectivity/reachability must not be read as logical inference and that multiple paths between two nodes must not be read as independent corroborating evidence — closing constraints preventing the graph representation from becoming an uncontrolled source of epistemic overclaiming.

anchor: Every epistemically relevant relation SHALL have an explicit semantic type. ... Statistical association SHALL NOT be represented as causation without a causal model or declared causal semantics.
statement: Twenty constitutional statements (IX-C1..IX-C20) close the Part: typed relations, direction preservation, no assumed algebraic properties (symmetry/transitivity/reflexivity), relation identity/provenance preservation, no entailment by mere connectivity, dependency explicitness and propagation rules, correlation/causation and temporal-precedence/causation separation, observation/intervention separation, relations themselves carrying revisable epistemic status, representable graph conflict, and explicit/inferred relation separation.

anchor: SUPERSEDED IN SUBSTANTIAL PART, 2026-09-06 ... The NOT READY verdict survives. Its reasoning does not.
statement: An added header notes the document is superseded in substantial part by a same-day re-verification, which found this document committed the error the corpus warns against (treating multiplicity of formulation as proof of non-resolution) in five places: the carrier (K_t is RATIFIED per the re-verification), Contr's explosion policy (non-explosion was ADOPTED), the ordering relation (complementary by adopted position; the 'FR-001 worsens the ordering' claim is withdrawn), equiv_sem (editorial), and dedup (explicitly outside the kernel); it also missed three items (Acknowledgment as a true absence, Reject<->I-12<->Article 8, and Pi in equiv?).

anchor: Does production code implement any kernel construct? No. ... A name collision, not an implementation.
statement: Self-verified (not inherited) findings: grep over app/ finds only two files, both an election-replay ReplayAssertion in the voting platform (a name collision with 'assertion', not a KnowledgeOS implementation); 'KnowledgeOsDoctor.php'-named scripts are repository diagnostics; 137 executable Python files are all research/verification experiments, not a kernel; existing code is evidence of an EKP-level platform and research programme, not of a KnowledgeOS kernel, and its absence is not evidence the theory is incomplete.

anchor: NOT COMPLETE, SPECIFIC CLOSING WORK REMAINS ... The dominant class is DECISION, not THEORY GAP
statement: Answers the mandate's six readiness questions: verifies and extends (rather than re-derives) the corpus's own prior gap-discovery register; the whole-system verdict is NO (boxed), classifying gaps into 3 genuine THEORY GAPs (dedup, empirical relational structure for measurement, source-independence), 7 unresolved DECISION gaps (the dominant class, matching CR-1..CR-5 plus OQ-1/OQ-2), several DERIVATION/INTEGRATION/SEMANTIC/COMPUTABILITY/SPECIFICATION gaps blocked behind the decisions, and a pure-engineering column implementable today.

anchor: 4 of 25 constructs carry no remaining blocker in any lane — Identity · Equality · Lineage · Orphan.
statement: A 25-construct readiness matrix (re-verified against the 2026-09-02 delta) shows only four constructs fully defined-and-implementable, with 25/25 having a formal definition but only 1/25 (Policy) in the ratified architectural surface, 0/25 with canonically defined operations or transformations.

anchor: The chain breaks at link 2 of 12 — CANONICAL CONCEPTS
statement: A 12-link dependency chain (Theory -> canonical concepts -> formal definitions -> invariants -> operations -> state transitions -> contracts/specs -> architecture -> implementation) is shown to break at the second link because four rival vocabularies exist for K with only an unratified characterized relation between two of them; every link below is downstream of that break plus five conflict records.

anchor: Five of the seven are GOVERNANCE ACTS, not derivations. ... A sub-kernel — hold a graph, compute lineage, check structural equality, detect orphans — is implementable today. It is not the KnowledgeOS kernel, and shipping it must not be reported as one.
statement: Names seven ordered blockers (the carrier OQ-1, Qualify's codomain CR-5, delta's argument type CR-3, Contr's signature/policy CR-1, the ordering relation CR-2, DECISION-02 OQ-2, and the equiv_sem naming CR-4) and states the programme is blocked on choices no derivation is entitled to make, not on mathematics it cannot do; explicitly distinguishes an implementable 'sub-kernel' (lineage/equality/orphan/identity) from the actual KnowledgeOS kernel and warns against reporting the former as the latter.

anchor: Inference Mechanism ≠ Inference Result ... Inference Result ≠ Truth ... Generated Hypothesis ≠ Established Knowledge.
statement: States Part X's central requirement: KnowledgeOS must preserve the distinction between what was observed, derived, estimated, hypothesized, or merely suggested, rather than treating any fluent or mathematically formatted reasoning output as authoritative.

anchor: I: (K,Γ,M,R,A) → O ... O = ⟨Premises,Conclusion,Rule,Model,Assumptions,Conditions,Uncertainty,Provenance,Status⟩.
statement: Formalizes inference as a typed operation with a rich, inspectable output structure rather than a bare conclusion, and requires deduction/induction/abduction/estimation/prediction to be distinguished as different semantic categories rather than one generic 'inference.'

anchor: Evidence ≠ Premise ≠ Inference ≠ Conclusion ≠ Determination ≠ Truth
statement: Closing constitutional chain of Part X (from twenty constitutional statements X-C1..X-C20 covering typed operations, direction/conditional preservation, deduction/statistical/defeasible/hypothesis/heuristic separations, no-automatic-truth and no-automatic-decision rules, conflict/multiple-path preservation, and gap-discovery via inference), preventing a reasoning engine from becoming authoritative merely by producing formatted output.

anchor: Number ≠ Quantity ≠ Measurement ≠ Meaning
statement: Central principle of Part XI: a bare numeral (e.g. 5) has almost no semantic meaning by itself (could be a count, a temperature, a score, a probability, a category code, an identifier); a quantity q=<value,dimension,unit,scale,context,time,provenance> is required to give it meaning.

anchor: Numerical zero SHALL NOT be conflated with contractual KnowledgeOS Zero.
statement: One of twenty constitutional statements (XI-C1..XI-C20) explicitly separates numeric 0 from the contract-relative epistemic Zero(K,EC) defined in Part V, alongside no-universal-arithmetic, estimand/estimator/estimate separation, missingness-vs-zero-vs-false-vs-unknown, and independence-not-inferred-from-distinct-identifiers rules.

anchor: Symbol → TypedValue → Quantity → Measurement → StatisticalObject → Inference → EpistemicInterpretation
statement: Closing principle of Part XI: a number acquires mathematical meaning only from its type, scale, model, context and provenance, via this explicit seven-stage chain, extending the deeper KnowledgeOS principle 'do not confuse the representation with the semantic statement' (5 vs 5kg vs 5kg±0.2kg vs thetahat=5 vs theta=5).

anchor: Temporal information is semantic information. ... Event Time ≠ Observation Time ≠ Knowledge Time ≠ Transaction Time ≠ Decision Time
statement: Worked example: a contract terminated 1 June but learned about on 15 June — replacing the event date with the discovery date changes the meaning of the knowledge, not merely its metadata; five distinct temporal dimensions must not be assumed to coincide.

anchor: A timestamp is a representation of temporal semantics, not temporal semantics itself.
statement: Formalizes time as a semantic domain tau with representation functions R_T:tau->Sigma_T (Unix/ISO-8601/calendar/logical-sequence/version-number), such that two representations can denote the same temporal object with different syntactic forms.

anchor: Temporal Zero means satisfaction of all required temporal constraints under the contract; it does not mean omniscience. ... Preserve when something happened, when it became known, and when the system recorded it as distinct facts whenever the contract requires those distinctions.
statement: Twenty constitutional statements (XII-C1..XII-C20) close the Part: event/knowledge/transaction-time non-substitution, temporal precision/uncertainty discipline, date-vs-instant, partial temporal ordering, logical-clock-not-physical-time, temporal precedence not establishing causality, and the explicit non-omniscient reading of 'Temporal Zero.'

anchor: Unknown ≠ Uncertain ≠ Probabilistic ≠ Risky ≠ Undetermined ≠ Undecided ... Probability ≠ Confidence ≠ Evidence ≠ Determination ≠ Decision.
statement: Central separation of Part XIII, illustrated by P(Loss)=0.8 not itself implying Decision=Avoid — decision also depends on consequences, alternatives, utility, constraints, preferences, authority, reversibility, timing and the decision contract.

anchor: Do not transform uncertainty into certainty merely because the system requires an answer. ... Do not treat uncertainty as ignorance when the uncertainty itself has been rigorously characterized.
statement: The Part's two complementary deepest principles, framing KnowledgeOS as aiming at 'contractually justified epistemic precision' rather than either artificial certainty or permanent skepticism.

anchor: AI-generated scores MUST NOT automatically be interpreted as probabilities. ... Contractual Zero MUST NOT be interpreted as elimination of all uncertainty.
statement: Two of twenty constitutional statements (XIII-C1..XIII-C20) explicitly targeting AI-score interpretation and reaffirming that contractual Zero (Part V) never means elimination of uncertainty, alongside confidence-interval/credible-interval non-substitution, model-vs-parameter uncertainty separation, and abstention/escalation support requirements.

anchor: Correlation(X,Y) ⇒ Cause(X,Y). That implication is generally false. ... TemporalPrecedence(X,Y) ⇏ Cause(X,Y). ... Prediction(Y∣X) ⇏ Cause(X,Y).
statement: Central warning of Part XIV against the invalid correlation/temporal-precedence/prediction -> causation inferences; requires an explicit causal model before any causal claim, distinguishing Association/Correlation/Prediction/Dependency/Causation/Explanation.

anchor: Non-identifiability MUST NOT be represented as zero effect. ... Confounding assumptions MUST NOT be silently resolved by statistical adjustment.
statement: Two of twenty constitutional statements (XIV-C1..XIV-C20) requiring explicit causal estimands and identification before treating a causal effect as determined, and forbidding silent conflation of an unidentifiable effect with a null effect.

anchor: "These things move together" ⇒ "This thing caused that thing." ... A causal claim is not a stronger description of a correlation; it is a different kind of knowledge requiring different semantics.
statement: Closing principle: the correct progression is Observation->Association->Hypothesis->CausalModel->Identification->CausalInference->Determination, and causality must not be represented as an ordinary graph edge when the domain requires causal-model semantics.

anchor: Model Output ≠ Observation ≠ Prediction ≠ Reality ... Possible ≠ Feasible ≠ Plausible ≠ Probable ≠ Expected ≠ Determined
statement: Central separation of Part XV: a model can be computationally correct while representing an inadequate model, a forecast can be statistically calibrated while wrong for an individual realization, and a scenario can be plausible without a meaningful probability.

anchor: M = ⟨V,S,Θ,A,Σ,Γ,Π,ν⟩
statement: Formalizes a model as a typed epistemic object (variables, structural relationships, parameters, assumptions, scope, context, preservation contract, validity function) rather than a bare function producing numbers.

anchor: Never promote a model-derived possibility into a stronger epistemic category without satisfying the contract that defines that category.
statement: Closing principle extending the corpus's core Evidence!=Truth!=...!=Action separation into future-oriented reasoning (Scenario!=Prediction!=Forecast!=Observation): the simulation does not become evidence because it is reproducible, the forecast does not become fact because its probability is high.

anchor: Knowledge ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Risk ≠ Decision ≠ Action ... Risk ≠ Probability.
statement: Central separation of Part XVI, illustrated by P(Loss)=0.8 not itself implying Decision=Avoid (decision depends also on consequences, alternatives, utility, constraints, authority, reversibility, timing, and the decision contract) and Risk requiring consequence semantics that mere probability under a model does not supply.

anchor: A good outcome does not prove that the decision process was good. ... A bad outcome does not by itself prove that the decision process was invalid.
statement: Two of twenty constitutional statements (XVI-C1..XVI-C20) explicitly forbidding outcome-based retrospective judgment of decision quality; decision evaluation must preserve the information available at decision time, and actual outcomes are not retroactively inserted into the historical decision state.

anchor: K_t → Decision_t → Action_t → Observation_{t+1} → K_{t+1}.
statement: Closes the Part by formalizing the full knowledge-to-action-and-back loop, stating that a decision is produced only when epistemic information is combined with consequences, preferences, constraints, authority and an explicit decision rule — knowledge, probability and risk do not decide by themselves.

anchor: Learning ≠ Accumulation ... Outcome → Learning does not automatically imply Outcome → Truth. ... ModelImprovement ≠ Truth.
statement: Central principle of Part XVII: learning is a controlled transformation of epistemic state resulting from new evidence, feedback, revised models, changed contracts or changed interpretations, not mere accumulation of records; feedback loops must not be allowed to silently manufacture truth.

anchor: K_0 → K_1 → K_2 → ⋯ → K_t ... with each transition preserving its reason, evidence, context, provenance, and governance.
statement: Closes Part XVII (and the seventeen-part rewrite so far) by recasting the central KnowledgeOS object as a fully-provenanced sequence of states rather than a single K, completing the learning loop Evidence->Evaluation->Learning->Model/Knowledge Change->Prediction->Decision->Action->Outcome->Evidence and warning that this loop must never become circular justification (a model's benchmark improvement does not make it universally true; a reduced gap does not make the system complete).

anchor: Training is not equivalent to learning. ... Concept drift is distinct from covariate shift. ... An observed outcome may generate evidence for revision but must not silently become truth.
statement: Twenty constitutional statements (XVII-C1..XVII-C20) separate training from learning, model evolution from knowledge evolution (contract-relative), concept drift from covariate shift, measurement drift from phenomenon change, semantic drift from schema change, and require historical model versions, update contracts, and rollback to preserve prior knowledge states.
